findings.title: Sudoers rule lets the operator run an operator-owned script as root
findings.description:
`MT_INSTALL` allows `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh --ref *` as root with no password. That path sits in the `manta` user's own checkout, so `manta` can edit the script and then run it as root. This is effectively unrestricted root, which contradicts the header comment ("nothing wider").

The `--ref *` argument is also an open wildcard. `mt-run *` and `systemctl ... mt-*` use the same open wildcard style. Sudoers `*` also matches spaces and slashes, so extra arguments can follow. Install the script to a root-owned path, or accept that this rule is full root and say so in the comment.

findings.title: Import ordering violates the required ruff `I` rule
findings.description:
The `cutover_common` import block puts `NOTES_DIR, fire_unit_until, start_log` ahead of `CutoverError, fire_unit, install, ...`, so it is not sorted. The same problem appears in these places:
- `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py`: `cagg_freshness_for_session` comes before `CheckReport`.
- `test/unit/test_repair_921.py`: `CaggFreshness, cagg_freshness_for_session, SymbolFindings` is unsorted.
- `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py`: the `minute_sessions` and `gaps.repair_921` imports come before `gaps.minute_coverage`.

`pyproject.toml` selects `I`, so `ruff check` should flag these.

findings.title: Extra pool connection opened per chunk while another is held
findings.description: `_do_minute_symbol` calls `pool.connection()` again for `fetch_session_bounds` inside its fetch loop. I did not confirm whether the outer `conn` is still held at that point. Nested checkouts risk pool exhaustion or deadlock when workers are concurrent, and every chunk now pays for an additional query. Reuse the existing connection if it is still held, or confirm the pool size and concurrency make this safe.

findings.title: Duplicated heavy mock setup in tests
findings.description: `test_last_bar_before_the_chunk_end_is_still_success` copies the roughly 60-line pool, transaction and patch scaffolding from `_run`. `_run` should take bounds, gap end and a logger option so the test can reuse it. Separately, the `[WAIT]` and `FAIL` checks in the cutover script match on substrings of printed text, which is fragile. Pre-existing code already does this for `FAIL`, and the diff extends it.

findings.title: Global log state and per-line file reopen
findings.description: `_LOG_FILE` is a module global, and `say` reopens the file on every call. This is acceptable for an operator script. Output from the raw `print` calls in `fire_unit_until` and `wait_for_unit_or_line` is not teed to the log, so the narration file is incomplete.
